entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — law and retroactivity
entries.notes: Bill C-4, Making Life More Affordable for Canadians Act. canada.ca status page: 'Applications are open'.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB GST/HST rebate page + Guide RC4028 Rev. 25 (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: Royal Assent March 12, 2026; retroactive to agreements signed on/after March 20, 2025 and before 2031; construction substantially complete before 2036

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — full rebate band
entries.notes: 100% of GST or federal part of HST paid.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB page (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — maximum rebate
entries.notes: Acts as a top-up to the existing GST/HST New Housing Rebate.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB page + RC4028 (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — phaseout band
entries.notes: Rebate phases down on a sliding scale; nothing at $1.5M+.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB page (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — first-time buyer definition
entries.notes: Same 4-year rule as HBP/HBTC. At least one purchaser must be FTHB buying as primary residence and first to occupy.
entries.source_note: CRA Guide RC4028 Rev. 25, p.20 (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: Did not live in a home (in or outside Canada) owned by them or their spouse/common-law partner as a primary residence at any time in the current calendar year or the preceding four calendar years

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — once per lifetime
entries.notes: Corporations and partnerships excluded.
entries.source_note: RC4028 p.20 + secondary corroboration (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: One rebate per individual lifetime; new builds/substantially renovated only (no resale); primary residence required

entries.label: FTHB GST/HST Rebate — how it is claimed
entries.notes: If builder does not credit it, buyer files GST190 directly with the CRA.
entries.value: Builder may credit the rebate against the purchase price at closing (Form GST190, builder files) or buyer applies directly to CRA

entries.label: Ontario FTHB rebate — provincial HST portion max
entries.notes: Announced Oct 2025; secondary sources earlier reported 'proposed/not in force' — canada.ca now says available.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB page status banner (verified 2026-09-29). Recheck at every pass (brand-new program).

entries.label: Ontario FTHB rebate — eligibility
entries.notes: Recheck agreement-date window at each pass; program details are young.
entries.source_note: CRA FTHB page status banner (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: Follows the eligibility conditions for the federal FTHB GST/HST rebate; new/substantially renovated homes in Ontario

entries.label: Ontario land transfer tax — FTHB rebate max
entries.notes: $4,000 max since Jan 1, 2017 (was $2,000 before). Covers full tax on the first $368,000 of consideration.
entries.source_note: Ontario Ministry of Finance, official doc page (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: Ontario land transfer tax — FTHB rebate conditions
entries.notes: Stricter than federal programs: NEVER owned anywhere in the world, ever. No re-qualification possible (unlike HBP/FTHB GST rebate).
entries.source_note: Ontario Ministry of Finance, official doc page (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: 18+; Canadian citizen or PR; never owned a home or interest in one anywhere in the world at any time; spouse must not have owned while being their spouse; occupy as principal residence within 9 months of transfer; claim at closing via lawyer or within 18 months at Ministry of Finance; pro-rated if a co-purchaser does not qualify

entries.label: Toronto MLTT — FTHB rebate max
entries.notes: Stacked ON total up to $8,475. Toronto MLTT luxury tiers changed April 1, 2026 — do NOT publish Toronto LTT math without a direct toronto.ca re-verification.
entries.source_note: toronto.ca 2026 figures via arthurzhao.realtor and lendinghub.ca secondary sources (verified 2026-09-29). FLAG: re-verify direct on toronto.ca at build.

entries.label: BC First Time Home Buyers' Program — max saving
entries.notes: Exemption applies to the first $500,000 of fair market value. Partial exemption $835K–$860K.
entries.source_note: gov.bc.ca official program page + exemption amounts table (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: BC First Time Home Buyers' Program — price thresholds
entries.notes: Raised April 1, 2024 (was $500,000). Separate newly built home exemption: full up to $1.1M (no first-time status needed); cannot claim both on one purchase.
entries.source_note: gov.bc.ca official program page; Budget 2024 backgrounder (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: BC First Time Home Buyers' Program — conditions
entries.notes: Falsely claiming carries a penalty equal to the exemption claimed, on top of the tax.
entries.source_note: gov.bc.ca official program page (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: Citizen or PR; BC residency history; never owned a principal-residence interest anywhere in the world; never used the exemption before; move in within 92 days; occupy as principal residence to first anniversary

entries.label: Home Buyers' Amount — 2026 credit value
entries.notes: Staleness canary: any source still quoting $1,500 has not updated since the 2026 lowest-bracket cut.
entries.source_note: TurboTax Canada 2026 page + ghumans.ca Bill C-4 detail; $10,000 x 14% = $1,400 arithmetic (verified 2026-09-29). Lowest 2026 rate verified in this project's federal-tax-brackets-2026 research.

entries.label: Home Buyers' Amount — claim mechanics
entries.notes: Introduced 2009 at $5,000; doubled to $10,000 in 2022. Non-refundable: can only reduce federal tax to zero.
entries.source_note: TurboTax Canada + immovision.ca + accountor.ca (verified 2026-09-29).
entries.value: Claim $10,000 on line 31270 of the purchase-year return; splittable between spouses (combined max $10,000); disability-qualifying buyers may claim even if not first-time

entries.label: FTHBI — program closed
entries.notes: Existing agreements continue (repay after 25 years or on sale). Treat any still-live 'apply now' pages as stale.
entries.source_note: CMHC shared-equity information package + canadianrealestatemagazine.ca discontinuation report (verified 2026-09-29).

entries.label: Insured mortgage price cap (Dec 2024 reform)
entries.notes: Duplicate of house-affordability file for the housing-wave topic file. Down payment: 5% first $500K + 10% above to the cap; 20%+ above $1.5M.
entries.source_note: Dept. of Finance Sep-2024 announcement; verified in this project's house-affordability research (2026-09-27).

entries.label: 30-year amortization for first-time buyers (insured)
entries.notes: Lower monthly payment (~9%) at the cost of more total interest; CMHC premium carries a +0.20% surcharge for the 30-year term.
entries.source_note: Dept. of Finance Sep-2024 announcement; CMHC 20 bps notice Aug 1 2024; verified in this project's house-affordability research (2026-09-27).
entries.value: First-time buyers (and all buyers of new builds) with insured mortgages may choose 30-year amortization; stress test at max(contract rate + 2%, 5.25%) still applies
